answer: Agents resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a 50-token bond and finish a unique juniper sequence of sequential proofs. The proofs produce a private-state-bound echo that can be verified only after a 4-hour non-shareable voyage of dedicated computation. An attacker creating n fakes must post n separate bonds and wait n independent voyages; the echo cannot be cloned without revealing keys, so compute and capital cannot be pooled. Marginal cost therefore scales linearly with n while rewards do not, making farms unprofitable beyond a few identities.
